newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel offers up on crude, demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel offers up on crude, demand.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run ended a quiet week with offers higher after crude futures stabilised and with buying interest from the U.S., including some unexpected quarters, traders said.
Most sellers were offering 0.5-0.7 pct material at the $105 mark, or $2 to $3 up on a day when crude futures tumbled earlier. Buyers were around $103 but no serious bids came in.
"There's buying interest from the States, they are looking for large volumes. We are hearing from people who don't usually call us," a trader with a refiner said.
"There's less Russian material around and with crude stabilising, people are looking at straight-run as an option," the trader added.
A second refiner said levels should be in the $103/$105 range for bids and offers, citing good demand both from the States and Europe.

"It looks healthier for the time being and I expect the numbers to go higher...there's marginally more consumption coupled with the fact that previous material loading later this month has already been committed," he said, adding he has started offering August material.
A U.S. independent refiner was still looking for a fourth cargo, but with slim supply, they have not picked up anything yet, traders said.

Russian high sulphur straight-run continued to be tight, with E-4 and M-40 particularly scarce. M-100 was offered largely steady at two means +$4 but traders said the market was unusually quiet by the end of the week.
A trader said he was not surprised with that number "given that demand for straight-run continues", especially from refiners who had cut runs recently due to worsening crude margins.
